so you couldn’t say your idol did it, that your carved image, your molten god commanded it.’ Is 48:3-5

but you still won’t own up to them;
now I’ll tell you things you haven’t heard.
7 They’re not things from long ago;
so you can’t claim you knew them all along.
8 I know what traitors you are;
you’ve been rebels from birth.
9 Yet for my name’s sake, I’ve delayed expressing my anger;
for my honor I’ve restrained it to keep from wiping you out.
10 I’ve refined you, but not like silver;
I’ve refined you in the furnace of suffering.
11 For my own sake—yes, I’ll do it for my own sake—
I won’t let my reputation be tarnished;
I won’t share my honor with idols. Is 48:6-11

The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says,
“Misfortune awaits Nebo—laid waste;
Kiriathaim will be disgraced—taken; the fortress will be humiliated—torn down.
2No more renown for Moab;
disaster’s in store for Heshbon
to cease being a nation!
Put Madmen to silence too;
chase it with a sword. Jer 48:1-2
3“An outcry from Horonaim,
‘Devastation and destruction!’
4Moab’s to be destroyed;
its little ones cry out in terror.
5At the ascent to Luhith, Moab’s refugees go up crying;
at the descent to Horonaim

6Run, save yourselves
so you can be a juniper in the countryside. Jer 48:3-6
7Because you trusted in your wealth and skill,
you’ll be captured too.
Chemosh will go into exile
with his priests and officials.
8A destroyer will come on every city;
no city will escape. The valley will perish;
the plateau will be destroyed like the LORD said.
9Give Moab wings so it can fly away;
its towns will be desolate without residents.
10A curse on the one that does the LORD’s work halfheartedly;
a curse on the one that restrains his sword from blood.
Jer 48:7-10
11“Moab hasn’t been disturbed since it was founded;
its dregs haven’t been unsettled.
It hasn’t been poured from jug to jug—
or carried into exile.
So it still tastes clean;
its aroma has body.

title: Jeremiah 48

content:
Psalms Chapter 48 A Song. A Psalm of the Sons of Korah
1 The LORD is great and deserves great praise
in the city of our God on his holy mountain.
2 Mount Zion, the heights of Zaphon, is high and beautiful—
the joy of the whole earth, the city of the great King.
3 In its towers God reveals himself as a strong defense.
4 Kings joined forces
and advanced against that strong defense.
5 But as soon as it came into view, they panicked and fled.
6 Panic seized them like the anguish of a woman in childbirth.
7 The LORD destroyed them
like ships of Tarshish capsized by an east wind.
8 As we’ve heard, so we’ve seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts, our God;
he’ll make it safe forever. Ps 48:1-8
9 In your Temple we think about your enduring love.
10 Like your name, God, your praise is everywhere;
your right hand is filled with goodness.
11 Let Mount Zion be happy,
and the residents of Judah celebrate your goodness.
12 Walk around Zion and count its towers;
13 inspect its ramparts and tour its fortresses
so you can tell the next generation;
14 because God is God forever;
he’ll guide us till we die.
Ps 48:9-14

Jeremiah Chapter 49 1 About Ammon
The LORD says,
“Doesn’t Israel have any descendants?
Doesn’t he have an heir?
Why then has Malcam/Milcom taken possession of Gad,
and his people settled in its towns?
2The time’s coming
when I’ll raise the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites.
It’ll be a desolate mound;
its towns will be burned,
Then Israel will expel the ones that expelled him. Jer 49:1-2
3“Wail, Heshbon, because Ai is destroyed!
Cry out, young women of Rabbah;
put on burlap and lament;
run back and forth inside the walls.
Malcam/Milcom will go into exile
along with his priests and officials.
4Why do you brag about your fertile valleys?
Your valleys are flowing away, unfaithful daughter
that trusts in her treasures and says,
‘Who’s going to attack me?’
5I’m going to bring terror on you
from every direction.
Every one of you will be driven out headlong
with nobody to round up the refugees.
6Yet later I’ll restore Ammon’s fortunes.” Jer 49:3-6

The LORD of Hosts says,
“Is there no wisdom in Teman?
Has good advice disappeared from the prudent?
Has its wisdom declined?
8Turn around, run away,
live deep in the deserts, people in Dedan,
because I’ll bring disaster on Esau when I punish him.
9If grape-gatherers come to you,
wouldn’t they leave some gleanings?

title: Jeremiah 49

content:
Psalms Chapter 49 For the Choir Director
A Psalm of the Sons of Korah
1 Hear this, every nation;
listen, everyone on earth,
2low and high, rich and poor alike.
3 My words are wise;
my thoughts are full of insight.
4 I listen to proverbs
and expound my riddles on a harp.
5 Why should I be afraid when there’s adversity,
when my enemies’ sins are all around me,
6people who trust in their wealth
and brag about how rich they are?
7 Nobody can use wealth to redeem a brother from death
or pay God a ransom for him—
8redeeming a life is too expensive;
you may as well forget about 9living on forever and not seeing the Pit.
Ps 49:1-9
10 Even the wise die—
just like the ignorant and senseless—
and leave their wealth to others.
11 They act like their houses will last forever,
like where they live will be there for all generations;
so they name their lands after themselves.
12 But in all their pomp, they won’t endure;
they’ll perish like animals. 13 This is the fate of the foolish and those who agree with them: 14like sheep they’re appointed to Sheol;
death will be their shepherd.
The godly will rule them in the morning;
Sheol will consume their form
far from their stately homes.
15 But God will redeem me from its power
and take me to himself. Ps 49:10-15
16 Don’t be afraid when people get rich,
when their houses appreciate in value;
17 because when they die, they won’t take anything with them;
what they gloried in won’t go down with them to the grave.
18 Though they congratulate themselves while they’re alive, though other people praise them for being successful,
19they’ll go to their ancestors
and never see the light of day. 20 People in all their pomp who don’t have intelligence
amount to being like animals when they die.
Ps 49:16-20

content:
Isaiah Chapter 50 Israel’s Sin and the Servant’s Obedience 50:1The LORD says,
“Did I put your mother away with divorce papers?
Did I sell you as slaves to pay my debts?
No, I sold you because of your transgressions and divorced your mother for her sins.
2 When I came, why wasn’t anybody home?
When I knocked, why didn’t anyone answer the door?
Am I too poor to pay a ransom;
don’t I have the strength to rescue?
I can dry up the sea with a word,
make rivers empty and the fish in them die and stink.
3 I dress the sky in darkness
and cover it with burlap.” Is 50:1-3
4 The Lord GOD has given me a disciple’s tongue
so I can comfort the weary with his message;
he wakes me up morning after morning
to help me understand his will.
5 He’s cleaned out my ears,
and I haven’t pulled away.
6 I’ve turned my back to the ones who scourge me
and my cheeks to those who pull out my beard;
I haven’t covered my face from being spit on.
7 He helps me so I’m not disgraced;
I set my face like flint
and know I won’t feel ashamed.
Is 50:4-7
8 The One that vindicates me is close at hand;
who wants to fight me?
Let’s stand up to each other.
Who wants to take me to court?
Go on, sue me!
9 The Lord helps me; who can condemn me?
Adversaries will wear out like old, moth-eaten clothes.
10 Who among you respects the LORD,
obeys his servant,
and still lives in the dark?
Trust the LORD and rely on him.
11 You that live by the light of the fires you set
will fall into them in torment. Is 50:8-11

content:
Jeremiah Chapter 51 1 The LORD says,
“I’m going to stir up the spirit of the destroyer
against Babylon and the people in Leb-kamai.
2 I’ll send foreign winnowers to Babylon to devastate its land.
On every side they’ll oppose it
at the time of its catastrophe.
3 Let the defending archer not bend his bow
or stand in his coat of mail.
Don’t spare the young men;
devote the whole army to destruction.
4 They’ll fall down dead in the land of the Babylonians,
pierced through in their streets.”
Jer 51:1-4
5 God, the LORD of Hosts,
has not abandoned Israel and Judah
even though their land is full of guilt
in front of the Holy One of Israel.
6 Escape from Babylon;
save yourselves!
Don’t get destroyed in its punishment;
this is the LORD’s revenge;
he’s going to render retribution to it.
7 Babylon has been a gold cup in the LORD’s hand,
intoxicating the whole region.
The nations have drunk its wine;
so they’re acting crazy. Jer 51:5-7
8 All of a sudden Babylon has fallen!
Wail for it!
Bring salve to heal its pain.
9 We tried to heal Babylon, but it didn’t heal;
so abandon it and get to your own country. Its judgment has reached heaven;
it towers as high as the sky.
10 The LORD has brought about our vindication;
let’s recount in Zion the work of the LORD our God!
Jer 51:8-10
11 Sharpen the arrows, fill the quills!
The LORD has stirred up the kings of the Medes
to destroy Babylon.
It’s the LORD’s revenge for his Temple. 12 Raise up a standard against the walls of Babylon;
post a strong guard, station sentries, set men in ambush!
It’s the LORD’s revenge for his Temple. 13 You that live by lots of water, abundant in treasures,
your end has come; your life cord’s been cut.
14 The LORD of Hosts has sworn by himself:
“I’ll fill you with soldiers like locusts;
they’ll raise shouts of victory over you.” Jer 51:11-14

Jeremiah Chapter 52 The Fall of Jerusalem 1 Zedekiah was 21 when he became king and ruled for 11 years in Jerusalem. His mother was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah. 2 He did all the evil Jehoiakim had done. 3 Because of the LORD’s anger over that, he put Jerusalem and Judah out of his presence.
Zedekiah revolted against the king of Babylon. 4 The tenth day, tenth month, ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar came with his army, set up camp against Jerusalem, and built a siege wall around it. 5 The city lay under siege till Zedekiah’s eleventh year. 6 The ninth day, fourth month, the famine was so severe in the city that the people didn’t have any food left. 7 Then they broke into the city, and the fighting men fled at night through the gate between the two walls by the king’s garden, even though the Babylonians were all around the city. They went toward the Arabah, 8 but the Babylonian army overtook the king in the plains by Jericho. His whole army scattered from him. 9 They captured him and took him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in Hamath, and he passed sentence on him. 10 He executed Zedekiah’s sons right in front of him and executed the officials of Judah. 11 Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with bronze bonds, and took him to Babylon. He put him in prison till his death.

content:
Psalms Chapter 52 For the Choir Director. A Maskil of David,
When Doeg the Edomite Came and Told Saul, “David has gone to Ahimelech’s house.”
1 God’s enduring love lasts all day;
so why brag about sinning, great soldier?
2 Your tongue cuts like a razor.
3 You like evil more than good,
falsehood more than truth. 4 You like words that devour and a lying tongue that deceives. 5 But God will strike you down once and for all;
he’ll pull you out of your tent
and uproot you from the land of the living.
Ps 52:1-5
6 Good people will see it and be amazed;
they’ll laugh at you and say,
7“Look at the men that wouldn’t take refuge in God,
but trusted in their great wealth
and used their strength to destroy.”
8 But I’m like a green olive tree in God’s house;
I’ll always trust in his enduring love. 9 I’ll be eternally grateful for what he’s done,
and depend on him in front of his holy people because that’s good.
Ps 52:6-9

content:
Isaiah Chapter 53 1 Who has believed our message?
Who has the LORD shown his arm to?
He grew up before the LORD like a tender sprout,
like a shoot out of parched ground.
2 He wasn’t particularly handsome or noble to draw our attention to him
or have the looks that would attract us to him.
3 People despised and abandoned him, a pained man, acquainted with grief;
like someone people look the other way from,
we looked down on him and didn’t respect him. Is 53:1-3
4 Actually though, he was shouldering our weaknesses
and carrying our pains,
but we considered him someone God struck and made suffer.
5 But he was pierced for our sins,
crushed for our iniquities.
The discipline that was for our welfare fell on him,
and by his scourging we are healed.
6 We’ve all wandered off like sheep
and turned to our own way;
but the LORD laid on him the sinfulness of us all. Is 53:4-6
7 He was oppressed and suffering,
but he didn’t say anything;
like a lamb they led to slaughter
or a sheep silent before its shearers,
he didn’t open his mouth.
8 He was taken away by oppression and condemnation;
who realized at the time
that he was being cut off from the living
for the sins of my people, who deserved the stroke?
9 They assigned his grave with criminals
though he hadn’t deceived or been violent; yet he was associated with a rich man in his death. Is 53:7-9
10 But it was the LORD’s plan to crush him,
to put him to grief;
when he offers himself as a guilt offering,
he’ll see his offspring and extend his life,
and the LORD will accomplish his good pleasure in him.
11 He’ll see what results from his anguish and feel fulfilled;
by his experience, my servant the upright one,
will justify many by shouldering their sins.
12 So God will assign him a place among the great,
and he’ll divide the spoil with the strong
because he poured out his life
when they treated him like a transgressor.
But he was shouldering many other people’s sins
and interceding for them. Is 53:10-12

Psalms Chapter 53 For the Choir Director. Set to Mahalath
A Maskil of David
1 Fools tell themselves there’s no God.
They’re corrupt and commit disgusting sins; none of them does what’s good.
2God looks down from heaven to see if anybody understands,
if anybody looks to him.
3Every one of them has turned aside and become corrupt;
not a one does what’s good, not a one [ Rom 3:10-12].
Ps 53:1-3
4 Won’t sinners ever learn?
They eat up my people like bread
and don’t pray to me.
5 They’ll be in a panic like never before,
because I’ll scatter the bones of your attackers;
you’ll put them to shame because I’ve rejected them.
6 Oh that deliverance would come out of Zion!
When I restore the fortunes of my people,
Jacob will celebrate, Israel will be happy.
Ps 53:4-6

content:
Isaiah Chapter 55 Invitation to the LORD’s Salvation 1 “Everyone that’s thirsty, come to the water;
you that don’t have any money, come, buy, and eat;
get wine and milk for free.
2 Why spend money on what’s not food,
wages on what doesn’t satisfy?
3 Come and listen so you can live;
I’ll make an everlasting covenant with you
like the faithful mercies I showed David.
4 I’ve appointed him as a witness to the nations,
a leader and commander for them.
5 You too will call nations you don’t know;
nations that don’t know you will hurry to you
because of the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel,
because he has honored you.” Is 55:1-5
6 Look for the LORD while you can find him;
call on him while he’s near.
7 Sinners need to change the way they act;
the unjust have to abandon selfish intentions.
They must return to the LORD
so he’ll have mercy on them,
come back to their God
because he’ll generously pardon.
8 “I don’t think like you do;
I don’t do like you do,” the LORD says.
9 “As high as the sky is above the earth,
my ways are above your ways
and my thoughts above your thoughts. Is 55:6-9
10 As rain and snow fall from the sky
and don’t go back there without watering the ground,
making it sprout and produce,
and providing seed to the sower and bread to the eater—
11 so my message won’t come back to me without accomplishing what I sent it to do.
12 You’ll go out with joy
and be led forth in peace;
the mountains and hills will break out in singing;
the trees in the field will clap their hands. 13 Cypress trees will come up in place of thorns;
myrtles will grow instead of nettles;
they’ll be a memorial to the LORD,
an everlasting sign that won’t be destroyed.” Is 55:10-13

2 Why spend money on what’s not food,
wages on what doesn’t satisfy?
3 Come and listen so you can live;
I’ll make an everlasting covenant with you
like the faithful mercies I showed David.
4 I’ve appointed him as a witness to the nations,
a leader and commander for them.
5 You too will call nations you don’t know;
nations that don’t know you will hurry to you
because of Yahveh your God, the Holy One of Israel,
because he has honored you.” Is 55:1-5
6 Look for Yahveh while you can find him;
call on him while he’s near.
7 Sinners need to change the way they act;
the unjust have to abandon selfish intentions.
They must return to Yahveh
so he’ll have mercy on them,
come back to their God
because he’ll generously pardon.
8 “I don’t think like you do;
I don’t do like you do,” Yahveh says.
9 “As high as the sky is above the earth,
my ways are above your ways
and my thoughts above your thoughts. Is 55:6-9
10 As rain and snow fall from the sky
and don’t go back there without watering the ground,
making it sprout and produce,
and providing seed to the sower and bread to the eater—
11 so my message won’t come back to me without accomplishing what I sent it to do.
12 You’ll go out with joy
and be led forth in peace;
the mountains and hills will break out in singing;
the trees in the field will clap their hands. 13 Cypress trees will come up in place of thorns;
myrtles will grow instead of nettles;
they’ll be a memorial to Yahveh,
an everlasting sign that won’t be destroyed.” Is 55:10-13

don’t ignore my plea.

trouble has overwhelmed me; I’m distracted 3by the threats of my enemies,
by bringing suffering on me

Ps 55:1-3

terror of death has fallen on me.

10 Day and night they patrol the walls,

I could handle that;

title: Psalms 55

content:
Isaiah Chapter 56 Blessings for All Nations 1 The LORD says,
“Maintain righteousness and be godly
because my salvation’s coming;
my deliverance will arrive.
2 They are fortunate who do that,
who hold onto it,
who honor my Sabbath
and don’t do anything sinful.
3 Foreigners that join themselves to the LORD shouldn’t say,
‘He’ll surely make a difference between me and his people’;
eunuchs shouldn’t say, ‘I’m a dead tree.’”
4 The LORD says,
“For eunuchs that keep my Sabbaths holy,
choose to do what pleases me,
and keep my covenant—
5 I’ll erect a memorial inside my Temple walls and inscribe on it a name that’s better than heirs. Is 56:1-5
6 “Foreigners that join me
to minister to me, love and serve me,
observe my Sabbaths, and keep my covenant—
7 I’ll bring to my holy mountain
and make happy in my Temple for prayer;
I’ll accept their sacrifices and burnt offerings on my altar;
I’ll make my Temple a house for prayer for all nations.”
8 The Lord GOD who brings back the dispersed from Israel, says,
“Still others I’ll bring to those I’ve already gathered.”
Is 56:6-8
Sinful Leaders Condemned 9 All you wild animals in the field and forest,
come and devour my people. 10 The watchmen are blind;
they don’t know what’s going on.
They’re dogs that can’t bark,
always lying around asleep, dreaming.
11 They have huge appetites they can never satisfy;
they’re shepherds that don’t know how to shepherd.
They’ve all turned to their selfish interests,
looking for personal profit.
12 “Come on,” they say, “let’s get some wine
and drink lots of alcohol;
tomorrow let’s do it again—and more so.” Is 56:9-12

content:
Psalms Chapter 56 For the Choir Director. A Mikhtam of David,
When the Philistines Seized Him in Gath
Set to The Pigeon in Far-Off Terebinths
1 Be gracious, God; people are walking all over me,
oppressing me all the time, 2attacking me.
3 When I’m afraid, I put my trust in you.
4 In you, whose word I praise, I’ve put my trust;
what can mortals do to me?
5 All day long they try to frustrate my purposes;
they think up ways to harm me.
6 They stir up conflict, they lurk, they watch my every step,
looking for a chance to kill me.
7 Because they’re sinful, throw them out;
in anger put them down, God! Ps 56:1-7
8 You’ve kept track of my wanderings
and collected my tears in your bottle;
aren’t they recorded in your scroll?
9 My enemies will retreat when I call to you for help;
I know this one thing: you’re with me.
10 In God, whose word I praise,
in the LORD, whose word I praise,
11I’ve put my trust so I won’t be afraid;
what can mortals do to me?
12 I have to perform my vows to you;
I’ll give thank offerings for your help,
13because you’ve delivered me from death
and my feet from stumbling
so I can walk with you in the light of life.
Ps 56:8-13

Isaiah Chapter 57 1 Good people perish and nobody notices;
the devout disappear without anyone realizing it,
because God takes good people out of harm’s way
2 They who take the godly road
go to peace and rest in their graves.
Idolatrous Worship Condemned 3 “But come here, you sons of sorcerers,
you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes.
4 Who are you making fun of?
Who are you mouthing off to?
Who are you sticking out your tongue at?
Aren’t you rebellious brats, lying cads
5 that worship your idols with lust among the terebinths
under every green tree,
that slaughter your children in the wadis
on the jagged rocks beneath the cliffs? Is 57:1-5
6 Your destiny is among those smooth-stone fertility symbols
that you worship in those wadis; they’re your fate;
you pour out liquid offerings to them
and make grain offerings;
am I supposed to be appeased by stuff like that?
7 You’ve committed adultery on every high mountain
and gone up there to offer sacrifice to your idols.
8 You’ve put pagan symbols on the back of your doors
and on your doorposts;
you’ve deserted me and uncovered yourself
to your Temple prostitutes;
you’ve loved their bed and looked at their nakedness. Is 57:6-8
9 You’ve gone to Molech with olive oil
and lots of perfume;
you’ve sent your messengers far and wide,
even to Sheol.
10 You’ve worn yourselves out by your long search,
but you didn’t give up;
you found renewed strength and didn’t faint. Is 57:9-10
11 “Who were you worried about and fearful of when you lied and didn’t think about me? 12 I’ll tell everybody about your so-called good deeds, but they won’t do you any good.
13 When you appealed for help, did your collection of idols deliver you?
A gust of wind can pick them up;
a breath can blow them over.
But whoever takes refuge in me will inherit the land
and possess my holy mountain.” Is 57:11-13

get rid of every obstacle to my people.”

raise your voice like a ram’s horn;
tell my people their transgressions.
2 They look to me daily and seem to delight to know my ways,
as if they’re a good nation that hasn’t left my ordinances;
they ask for favorable verdicts
and act like they delight in drawing near to me.
3 Then they wonder, ‘Why have we fasted, and you haven’t noticed?
Why have we humbled ourselves, and you haven’t acknowledged it?’
It’s because you fast to get what you want
(meanwhile overworking your workers)! Is 58:1-3
4 You fast only to win disputes and fist fights—
not to be heard on high.
5 Is that the kind of fast I had in mind for humbling yourselves?
Isn’t that just going through the motions of bowing your head like a reed
and spreading out burlap and ashes under you?
Do you call that penance, a fast that’s acceptable to the LORD?
6 Isn’t this the kind of fast I had in mind:
loosening the bonds of people you falsely imprisoned,
undoing the straps of their yoke,
freeing the oppressed,
and breaking every ties that binds people? Is 58:4-6
7 Isn’t it sharing your food with the hungry,
bringing the homeless into your house,
dressing the naked when you see them,
not hiding from relatives that need you?
8 Then your light will break forth like the dawn;
your wounds will heal quickly.
Your good reputation will precede you;
the glory of the LORD will have your back.
9 You’ll call and he’ll answer;
you’ll appeal to him, and he’ll say, ‘I’m here.’
If you remove oppression from among you,

quench your thirst,
and restore your strength;
he’ll make you like an irrigated garden,
like a year-round spring.

on foundations from long ago;

content:
Psalms Chapter 58 For the Choir Director. A Mikhtam of David
Set to Do Not Destroy
1 Leaders, do you decree what’s right?
Do you judge justly?
2 No, you plot injustice in your hearts
and spread violence in the land.
3 The sinful go astray from the womb;
they lie from the time they’re born.
4 They have venom like vipers,
and stop up their ears like deaf cobras
5so they don’t hear their charmers’ voices
or those skilled at casting spells.
Ps 58:1-5
6 Pull out their fangs, God;
break the teeth out of the young lions.
7 Make them disappear like water that drains away;
make their arrows shafts without points.
8 Make sinners be like snails that dissolve as they go along,
like a miscarriage that never sees the sun.
9 Before your pots can feel the heat of burning briers;
he’ll sweep them away with a whirlwind,
whether green or on fire.
Ps 58:6-9
10 Good people will celebrate when they see God pay them back;
he’ll wash their feet in the sinners’ blood.
11 People will say, “There’s surely a reward for good people;
there’s certainly a God that judges on earth!”
Ps 58:10-11

content:
Psalms Chapter 59 For the Choir Director. A Mikhtam of David,
When Saul Sent Men to Watch the House and Kill Him
Set to Do Not Destroy
1 Deliver me from my enemies, God;
set me on high away from my attackers.
2 Save me from sinners;
rescue me from bloodthirsty people.
3 They lie in ambush to kill me;
fierce enemies stir up conflict against me, LORD, but not for my transgression.
4 For no fault of mine, they run to attack me;
get up to see and help me! Ps 59:1-4
5 LORD God of Hosts, God of Israel,
wake up and punish the nations;
don’t extend grace to any that are treacherous.
6 They come back in the evening and roam the city, howling like dogs.
7They growl with their mouth;
they have swords in their lips;
they say, “Who’s going to hear us?”
8 But you laugh at them, LORD;
you scoff at the nations.
Ps 59:5-8
9 I’ll watch for you, my Strength, my fortress.
10 You’ll meet me in your enduring love;
and let me look down in triumph at my enemies.
11 Don’t kill them; otherwise, my people will forget;
scatter them with your power
and bring them to their knees, LORD our shield.
12 For the sin of their mouth and the words of their lips,
catch them in their pride, their curses, and the lies they tell.
13 In your anger, destroy them so they’ll be out of the way,
so people will know that you rule in Jacob
and everywhere. 14 They come back in the evening and roam the city, howling like dogs.
15 They wander around looking for food
and growl if they’re not satisfied.
Ps 59:9-15
16 But I’ll sing about your strength,
every morning about your enduring love.
You’ve been my fortress,
my refuge in trouble.
17 I’ll sing praise to you, my Strength,
the God who shows me enduring love. Ps 59:16-17

content:
Isaiah Chapter 60 Israel’s Future Glory 1 “Arise, shine; your light has come;
the glory of the LORD has risen on you.
2 Darkness will cover the earth;
thick blackness will blanket the nations;
but the LORD will shine on you;
his glory will appear on you.
3 Nations will come to your light,
kings to the brightness of your rising. Is 60:1-3
4 “Look all around you;
they’re all gathering home to you.
Your little boys will come from a long way off;
your girls will be carried in arms.
5 Then your eyes will be radiant;
you’ll be thrilled and happy,
because commerce from the sea will return to you,
and the nations’ wealth will be available to you.
6 Caravans of camels will cover you,
young camels from Midian and Ephah.
The ones from Sheba will bring gold and frankincense,
and good news about the praises of the LORD.
7 The flocks of Kedar will gather to you;
the rams of Nebaioth will serve you.
I’ll accept them on my altar
and honor my Temple.
8 Who are these that fly like a cloud,
like pigeons to their windows? Is 60:4-8
9 The distant lands will learn to trust in me;
the ships from Tarshish will come first,
bringing your descendants home from afar
and their silver and gold with them
for the LORD your God,

content:
Psalms Chapter 60 For the Choir Director. A Mikhtam of David,
to teach when he struggled with Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab came back and struck 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt
1 You’ve rejected us, God, and broken us;
you’ve been angry, but restore us now.
2 You’ve made the land quake; you’ve split it open;
now repair the faults and stop the tremors.
3 You’ve made your people endure hardship
and given us wine that makes us stagger.
4 You’ve raised a banner for those who respect you
as a rallying point for truth. 5 Save us now with your right hand and answer us,
deliver your beloved.
Ps 60:1-5
6 In his kindness God has answered;
“I’ll celebrate by dividing up Shechem
and measuring out the Valley of Succoth.
7 Gilead and Manasseh belong to me;
Ephraim is my helmet; Jacob is my scepter.
8 Moab will be my washbasin;
I’ll scrape off my shoes on Edom
and shout in triumph over Philistia!”
Ps 60:6-8
9 Who will take me to a fortified city?
Who will lead me to Edom?
10 Have you rejected us, God?
You’re not going out with our armies.
11 Help us against our enemies;
we have no hope of human deliverance!
12 Through you we can do valiantly;
you’ll tread down our adversaries.
Ps 60:9-12

content:
Isaiah Chapter 61 The Year of the LORD’s Favor 1 The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on me;
he’s anointed me to bring good news to the downtrodden.
He’s sent me to bandage up the brokenhearted,
to liberate captives,
to free prisoners,
2 to announce that this is the year the LORD shows blessing,
the day he sets things right,
to comfort anyone that’s grieving,
3 to give to the sad in Zion
a crown in place of ashes,
the oil of happiness instead of mourning,
the mantle of praise rather than a fainting spirit
so they’ll be like Terebinths of Goodness
the LORD has planted to demonstrate his glory. Is 61:1-3
4 Then they’ll rebuild the ancient ruins,
set back up what was torn down,
repair destroyed towns deserted for generations.
5 Foreigners will pasture your flocks,
do your farming, and tend your vineyards.
6 But you’ll be the LORD’s priests;
people will speak of you as his ministers.
You’ll feed on the wealth of nations
and take pride in their prosperity. 7 Instead of humiliation you’ll have a double portion;
rather than dishonor you’ll celebrate over your lot.
You’ll have everlasting joy in your land.
8 “I, the LORD, love justice
and despise short-changing in burnt offering;
I’ll make an everlasting contract with you
and faithfully pay you for your work.
9 Then the nations will honor your offspring worldwide;
everyone will recognize you as the offspring the LORD blessed.” Is 61:4-9
10 I’m really happy in the LORD;
I celebrate over my God
because he’s dressed me in salvation
and wrapped me in goodness like a robe, like a groom dresses himself in a garland,
and a bride adorns herself with jewels.
11 As the ground produces seeds
and a garden makes sprouts grow,
so the Lord GOD makes goodness and praise
spring up for all the world to see. Is 61:10-11

Psalms Chapter 61 For the Choir Director. A Psalm of David
On Stringed Instruments
1 Listen to my prayer, God; hear my prayer.
2 With a faint heart I call to you from the end of the earth;
lead me to the rock that’s higher than me.
3 You’re my refuge, my strong tower against the enemy.
4 Let me live in your tent forever
and take shelter under your wings. 5 You’ve heard my vows, God,

make his lifetime like many generations.

appoint enduring love and truth to preserve him.
8 I’ll sing praise to you forever
as I pay my vows each day.

content:
Isaiah Chapter 62 Isaiah’s Prayer for Jerusalem 1 For Zion’s sake I’ll speak to God;
for Jerusalem’s sake I won’t keep still,
until your goodness glows brightly,
and your salvation radiates like a burning torch;
2 so the nations can witness your goodness
and kings can gaze at your glory.
The LORD himself will give you a new name.
3 You’ll be a beautiful crown in his hand,
a royal diadem he holds up high.
4 You won’t be called Abandoned [Azubah] anymore
or your land be named Desolate [Shemamah];
you’ll be My Delight Is in It [Hephzibah],
and your land will be Married [Beulah],
because he delights in you,
and your land will be married to him.
5 Like a young man marries a virgin,
your sons will marry you, Jerusalem;
like a groom is happy over a bride,
your God will be happy over you. Is 62:1-5
6 I’ve stationed watchmen on your walls, Jerusalem,
not to be silent day or night,
but to remember you to the LORD
7 till he makes you something worth praising in the world.
8 He has sworn by his right hand and strong arm,
“I’ll never again let your enemies eat your grain
or foreigners drink the new wine you labored for.
9 But the ones that put the grain in the granary will eat it and praise me;
the ones that pick the grapes will drink the wine in the courts of my sanctuary.”
Is 62:6-9
10 Go out through the gates; clear the way for my people.
Build a highway so they can return; get the loose rocks off the road. Hoist a flag the nations can see.
11 The LORD has declared all over the world,
“Tell Zion its salvation’s coming;
he’s bringing his reward with him.”
12 They’ll call you The Holy People [Ha‘am Haggadosh], The LORD’s Redeemed [Ge’ule-adonai],
The Sought For, A City No Longer Forsaken. Is 62:10-12

Isaiah Chapter 64 64:1Oh that you’d open the sky and come down
and the mountains would quake in your presence—
2 like a flame that burns brush and boils water—
to show yourself to your adversaries
so they’d tremble in your presence!
3 When you did awesome things we didn’t expect,
you came down and the mountains quaked in your presence.
4 No one has ever heard of a God like you
that acts on behalf of people that wait for him.
5 You visit those who enjoy doing good,
who remember you and your ways.
You were angry because we kept sinning for a long time;
can we ever be saved?
6 We’ve all become unclean; our best efforts are like menstrual rags.
We wither like leaves;
our sins blow us away like the wind.
7 No one calls on you or reaches out to you
because you’ve hid from us
and delivered us to the consequences of our sins. Is 64:1-7
8 But now, LORD, you’re our Father;
we’re the clay, you’re the potter;
you’ve made us.
9 Don’t be angry beyond measure;
don’t hold our sin against us forever;
look now, we’re all your people.
10 Your holy cities have become a desert;
Zion is a wasteland;
Jerusalem is desolate.
11 Our holy, beautiful Temple,
where our ancestors praised you,
has been burned;
all our precious things lie in ruins.
12 Will you limit yourself to this much retribution, or will you keep disciplining us no end? Is 64:8-12

content:
Psalms Chapter 64 For the Choir Director. A Psalm of David
1 Listen to my complaint, God;
keep me from living in dread of my enemies.
2 Hide me from the secret plots of bad people,
from the schemes of sinners
3that sharpen their tongue like a sword,
that aim bitter words like arrows,
4that shoot at innocent people from hiding places [Jn 15:25],
and do it suddenly without qualms.
5 They latch onto sinful purposes
and talk secretly about setting traps;
they say, “Who will notice?”
6 They look for ways to be unjust, “We’re ready with a well-conceived plot,”
because the human mind and heart are cunning.
Ps 64:1-6
7 But God will wound them with an arrow 8and make them trip over their tongues!
Everybody that sees them will shake their heads.
9 Then everybody will be respectful
and talk about what God’s done
and ponder what he’s made.
10 Good people will be happy in the LORD
and take refuge in him;
the godly in heart will honor him. Ps 64:7-10

Isaiah Chapter 65 Judgment and Final Salvation 65:1“I let people look for me who weren’t asking about me;
people that weren’t looking for me found me.
I said, ‘I’m here! Over here!’
to people that didn’t call on me.
2 All day long I spread out my hands to a rebellious nation
that follows its own ideas,
3 that continually angers me to my face
by offering sacrifices to idols in sacred gardens and burning incense on pagan altars,
4 that sit in tombs and spend the night in secret places,
that eat pig meat
and have broth from unclean meat in their pots,
5 that say, ‘Stay away from me;
don’t touch me;
I’m holier than you are!’ They’re smoke in my nose, a fire that burns all day. Is 65:1-5
6 I’ve written it out in front of me:
I won’t stand idly by; I’ll repay.
I’ll pay back into their laps
7 the sins they and their ancestors committed;
since they’ve burned incense on the mountains
and scorned me on the hills, I’ll measure out their former deeds into their arms,”
the LORD says.
8 “As new wine comes from clusters
and somebody says, ‘Don’t ruin it; it’s useful’;
that’s what I’ll do with my servants and not destroy them all.
9 I’ll preserve a remnant from Jacob and Judah
to inherit my mountains;
my chosen ones will inherit it;
my servants will live there. Is 65:6-9
10 Sharon will be a pasture for flocks;
the Valley of Achor will be a resting place for herds—
for my people that look to me.
11-12 But I’ll destine for the sword you that leave me,
that forget my holy mountain,
that set a table for Fortune

“My servants will eat, but you’ll be hungry;
my servants will drink, but you’ll be thirsty;
my servants will celebrate, but you’ll be humiliated;

content:
Psalms Chapter 66 For the Choir Director. A Psalm. A Song
1 Make a joyful sound to God, all the earth.
2 Sing about his honor;
make his praise glorious.
3 Say to him, “What you do is so awesome!
Your enemies feign obedience to you
out of fear for your power.
4 All the earth worships you and praises you;
they sing praises to you.” Ps 66:1-4
5 Come and see what God has done;
it’s awesome what he’s done for people.
6 He turned the Red Sea into dry ground;
the people crossed through the Jordan on foot;
they celebrated over him there.
7 He rules by his power forever;
he keeps watch over the nations;
the rebellious don’t make an uprising. Ps 66:5-7
8 Bless our God, you nations;
sound his praise abroad.
9 He keeps us alive
and doesn’t let our feet slip.
10 You’ve tried us, God,
and refined us like silver.
11 You caught us in your net
and laid a heavy load in our lap.
12 You put a ruler over us
and passed us through fire and water;
yet you brought us out into a large place.
13 I’ll come to your Temple with burnt offerings
and keep the vows 14 I made when I was in trouble.
15 I’ll offer you burnt offerings of healthy animals
with the smoke of rams;
I’ll offer bulls and male goats. Ps 66:8-15
16 Come and listen, you that respect God,
and I’ll tell you what he’s done for me.
17 I appealed to him with my mouth and extolled him with my tongue.
18 If I cherish sinfulness in my heart,
the LORD won’t hear me.
19 But he’s certainly heard me;
he’s listened to my prayer.
20 Bless God,
who hasn’t ignored my prayer
or withdrawn his enduring love.
Ps 66:16-20

5 Come and see what God has done;
it’s awesome what he’s done for people.
6 He turned the Red Sea into dry ground;
the people crossed through the Jordan on foot;
they celebrated over him there.
7 He rules by his power forever;
he keeps watch over the nations;
the rebellious don’t make an uprising. Ps 66:5-7

sound his praise abroad.
9 He keeps us alive
and doesn’t let our feet slip.
10 You’ve tried us, God,
and refined us like silver.
11 You caught us in your net
and laid a heavy load in our lap.
12 You put a ruler over us
and passed us through fire and water;
yet you brought us out into a large place.

and keep the vows 14 I made when I was in trouble.

with the smoke of rams;
I’ll offer bulls and male goats. Ps 66:8-15

and I’ll tell you what he’s done for me.

he’s listened to my prayer.

who hasn’t ignored my prayer
or withdrawn his enduring love.

chase off those who hate you!

Psalms Chapter 70 For the Choir Director. A Psalm of David
for a Memorial
1 Hurry and deliver me, LORD;
come quick to help me.

don’t let me be discredited.
2 In your goodness, rescue me;
listen to me and save me.
3 Be my rock of refuge that I can always go to;
give orders to save me
because you’re my rock and fortress.
4 Rescue me from sinners,
from the grasp of cruel men.
5 You’re my hope, Lord GOD,
my confidence since I was young.

and sustained me since I was born. Ps 71:1-6
7Many have marveled over me
because you’ve been my strong refuge.
8 I’m full of your praise and glory all the time.
9 Don’t set me aside in my old age
or leave me as my strength begins to fail.
10 My enemies speak against me;
they who want to kill me consult with each other,
11“God has left him.
Let’s go get him; he doesn’t have anybody to defend him.”
Ps 71:7-11
12 God, stay close by to help me.
13 Consume my adversaries with shame;
cover their faces with dishonor that try to harm me.
14 But I’ll keep hoping and praising you on and on.
15 I’ll tell about your goodness
and how many times you’ve saved me,
though I can’t count how often that’s happened.
16 I’ll praise the great deeds of the Lord GOD
and tell about the goodness you alone have.

I still talk about your wonderful deeds.
18 Even when I’m old and grey, don’t leave me, LORD,
till I tell this generation about your strength
and future people about your power.

title: Psalms 71

content:
Psalms Chapter 72 A Psalm of Solomon 1 Give the king your judgments, God;
give your goodness to his son.
2 May he judge your people fairly,
your oppressed ones with justice.
3 Let the mountains bring prosperity to the people;
may the hills bring goodness.
4 May he defend the downtrodden,
save the children of the needy,
and crush their oppressors. Ps 72:1-4
5 Let them respect you as long as the sun lasts,
as long as the moon endures—throughout all generations.
6 May the king rule like rain on mown grass,
like showers that water the ground.
7 May good people flourish in his time
and have abundant peace till the moon disappears.
Ps 72:5-7
8 May he rule from sea to sea, from the Euphrates River to the ends of the earth.
9 Let desert nomads bow to him,
and his enemies lick dust.
10 Let the kings of Tarshish and the islands bring presents,
and the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.
11 Let all kings bow to him
and every nation serve him.
12 He’ll deliver the needy when they call for help,
the oppressed with no one to help them.
13 He’ll have mercy on the poor and needy
and save their lives.
14 He’ll rescue them from oppression and violence;
their blood is precious to him;
15 so may they live long and receive the gold of Sheba;
let them pray to him continually
and bless him all day long.
Ps 72:6-15
16 May grain be abundant in the land;
may it wave on tops of the hills.
May it produce like Lebanon;
may its people blossom in the city like grass in the pasture.
17 May the king’s name last forever
and grow as long as the sun shines.
Let people bless themselves by him
and all nations call him blessed.
18 Bless the LORD, the God of Israel,
who alone does wonderful things.
19 Bless his glorious name forever;
may the whole world be full of his glory.
Amen and Amen. 20 The end of the prayers of David son of Jesse Ps 72:12-20

Psalms Chapter 73 BOOK 3 A Psalm of Asaph
1 God is good to Israel, to those whose hearts are pure.
2 I’d almost stumbled; my steps almost slipped;
3because I envied the prosperity of the arrogant.
4 They don’t seem to suffer when they die;
their bodies are healthy and well.
5 They don’t have trouble like other people;
they aren’t stricken like everyone else.
6 So pride is the gold chain around their neck;
violence is their clothes.
7 Their eyes are puffy with fatness;
they have everything they could want.
8 They mock, and talk about oppressing,
and talk down to the oppressed.
9 They brag against the sky itself;
their words strut across the world.
Ps 73:1-9
10 So his people turn to them
and drink in all their claims.
11 They say, “How does God know any of this?
Does the Most High even know what’s happening?”
12 They’re the sinful,
always at ease as their wealth grows.
13 It seems like I’ve kept my heart pure for nothing
and washed my hands in innocence for no reason,
14because I’m stricken all day and endure grief every morning.
Ps 73:10-14
15 If I’d talked the way I felt,
I’d have betrayed your people.
16 When I tried to understand why sinners prosper,
I was troubled by it
17 till I went to God’s sanctuary;
then I understood their destiny.
18 You put them on slippery places
and make them slide into ruin.
19 They’re quickly destroyed,
completely swept away by sudden desolation!
20 They’re like dreamers when they wake up, LORD;
their phantoms disappear.
Ps 73:15-20

like an animal in your presence.

I want you more than anything on earth.
26 My own flesh and heart may grow weak,
but you’re my strength and portion forever.

you destroy those who are not faithful to you.

Why does your anger smoke at the sheep in your pasture?
2 Remember your community that you bought so long ago,
that you redeemed as a tribe for your heritage,
Mount Zion, where you’ve lived.

the enemy has destroyed everything in the sanctuary.

and set up their own standards for signs.

7 They burned the sanctuary to the ground
and defiled your home.
8 They said to themselves, “We’ll completely subdue them”;
they set fire to your meeting places in the land.
9 We don’t see miraculous signs anymore;
there aren’t any prophets;
nobody knows how long this will last.
10 How long will your adversaries scoff, God,
and mock you? Forever?
11 Why hold back from doing something?
Why keep your right hand against your chest?

who provided deliverance on the earth.

content:
Psalms Chapter 76 For the Choir Director. A Psalm of Asaph
A Song. On Stringed Instruments
1 God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel.
2 His home is in Salem; he lives on Zion.
3 He has broken flaming arrows there,
shields, swords, and weapons of war.
4 You’re glorious, more majestic than mountains full of beasts of prey.
5 Our stouthearted enemies have been stripped of their spoil;
they’ve sunk into deep sleep;
none of the soldiers could raise a hand against us.
6 At your rebuke, God of Jacob,
horse and rider were thrown down into dead sleep.
7 You’re to be respected;
who can withstand you when you’re angry?
Ps 76:1-7
8 You rendered judgment from heaven; the earth lay silent in fear
9when you arose to measure out judgment,
to save the oppressed on earth. 10 People’s wrath only heightens your honor;
you dress yourself with the ashes of their anger.
11 Make your vows to the LORD your God and fulfill them;
let everyone bring gifts to the One they need to respect.
12 He breaks the pride of princes;
kings on earth respect him.
Ps 76:8-12

content:
Psalms Chapter 77 For the Choir Director. A Psalm of Asaph
Set to Jeduthun
1 I raise my voice up to God; I call out loud;
it rises to him so he’ll hear me.
2 When trouble comes, I turn to the LORD for help.
All night I reach out to him,
but I get no reassurance.
3 When I think about him, I’m shaken;
I sigh and feel faint.
4 He won’t let me sleep;
I’m in such distress I can’t pray.
5 I think about days gone by, years ago.
6 I remember singing during the night,
meditating and pondering in my mind. Ps 77:1-6
7 Will the LORD reject me forever now?
Won’t he ever be kind to me again?
8 Has his enduring love stopped permanently?
Have his promises come to an end?
9 Has he forgotten to be gracious?
In his anger has he withdrawn his mercy? 10 I said, “It’s my destiny
that the LORD has turned against me.”
11 Then I reconsider what all you’ve done, LORD,
and recall your wonders from of old.
12 I think about everything you do.
13 Your way is holy;
What god is as great as you?
14 You work wonders
and demonstrate your power among the nations.
15 You’ve rescued your people by your strength,
descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Ps 77:7-15
16 When the water faced you, God, it tremored to its depths.
17 Clouds poured down water;
the sky thundered; your arrows flashed.
18 You thundered in the whirlwind;
lightning flashes lit up the landscape;
the ground shook.
19 You went through the sea;
your path led into deep water,
but your footprints didn’t show.
20 You led your people like a flock
by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
Ps 77:16-20

that Yahveh has turned against me.”
11 Then I reconsider what all you’ve done, Yahveh,
and recall your wonders from of old.
12 I think about everything you do.
13 Your way is holy;
What god is as great as you?
14 You work wonders
and demonstrate your power among the nations.
15 You’ve rescued your people by your strength,
descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Ps 77:7-15
16 When the water faced you, God, it tremored to its depths.
17 Clouds poured down water;
the sky thundered; your arrows flashed.
18 You thundered in the whirlwind;
lightning flashes lit up the landscape;
the ground shook.
19 You went through the sea;
your path led into deep water,
but your footprints didn’t show.
20 You led your people like a flock
by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
Ps 77:16-20

title: Psalms 78

content:
Psalms Chapter 79 A Psalm of Asaph
1 Other nations have invaded your inheritance, God;
they’ve defiled your holy Temple
and laid Jerusalem in ruins.
2 They’ve given the buzzards your servants’ corpses,
and the wild animals the flesh of your holy people.
3 They’ve poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem;
there wasn’t anybody to bury them.
4 We’ve become a disgrace to our neighbors,
mocked and derided by the people around us.
5 LORD, will you be angry forever?
Will your jealousy keep burning like fire?
Ps 79:1-5
6 Pour out your wrath on nations that don’t know you,
that don’t call on you;
7they’ve devastated Jacob and laid waste his realm.
8 Don’t hold our ancestors’ sins against us;
bring us mercy quickly because we’re in despair.
9 For your honor, help us, God who delivers;
forgive our sins for your name’s sake. 10 Why should the nations say, “Where’s their God?”
Show those nations your vengeance
for your servants’ blood that they shed.
11 Listen to the moaning prisoner;
with your great power save those doomed to die.
12 Repay our neighbors seven times over for the taunts they’ve leveled at you, LORD,
13so we, your people, the sheep in your pasture,
can be eternally grateful to you
and recount your praise to all generations. Ps 79:6-13

content:
Psalms Chapter 80 For the Choir Director. A Psalm of Asaph
Set to Lilies; A Testimony
1 Listen, Shepherd of Israel,
you that lead Joseph like a flock;
show your glory, you that are enthroned above the cherubs.
2 Stir up your power against Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh;
and come to rescue us.
3 Restore us, God; look at us with favor so we’ll be saved. Ps 80:1-3
4 LORD God of Hosts,
how long will you be angry with our prayers?
5 You’ve fed us tears
and made us drink them in full measure.
6 You made us a taunt to our neighbors;
they laugh at us among themselves.
7 God of Hosts, restore us; look at us with favor so we’ll be saved. Ps 80:4-7
8 You took a grapevine out of Egypt,
drove out the Canaanite nations,
and planted it in their land.
9 You cleared the ground for it;
it took deep root and spread across the whole land.
10 It covered the mountains with its shadow
and God’s cedars with its branches.
11 It grew its branches all the way out to the Mediterranean Sea,
its shoots as far as the Euphrates River.
12 Why did you tear down its walls
so everybody that goes by can pick its fruit?
13 A boar from the woods roots it up;
whatever moves in the countryside feeds on it. Ps 80:8-13
14 God of Hosts, please come back now;
look down from heaven and take care of this grapevine,
15 the root you planted,
the son you’ve raised for your use.
16 Our enemies have cut it down and burned it;
may they perish at the rebuke from your angry look. 17 Encourage the man at your right hand,
the son you made strong for yourself.
18 Then we won’t turn away from you anymore;
revive us so we can call on you again.
19 LORD God of Hosts, restore us;
look at us with favor so we’ll be saved. Ps 80:14-19

content:
Psalms Chapter 81 For the Choir Director. A Psalm of Asaph Set to The Gittith
1 Sing to God your Strength;
make a joyful sound to Jacob’s God.
2 Sing, beat the tambourine,
pluck the lyre and harp.
3 At the new moons blow your ram’s horn,
at the full moon and on your festival days.
4 It’s a statute for Israel,
an ordinance from Jacob’s God.
5 He established it as a Testimony in Joseph
when he displayed his power all over Egypt.
I heard a language I didn’t know, saying. Ps 81:1-5
6 “I’ll take the burden off your shoulders
and free you from heavy labor.
7 You cried out in trouble, and I rescued you;
I answered you while I concealed myself in a thundercloud;
I tested you when you had no water at Meribah. 8 Listen, my people, when I admonish you;
Israel, if only you’ll listen!
9 There’s to be no foreign god among you;
don’t worship any alien deity.
10 I’m the LORD your God
who brought you out of Egypt.
Open your mouth, and I’ll fill it.” Ps 81:6-10
11 “But my people ignored me;
Israel wouldn’t obey.
12 So I let them follow their stubborn heart
and go after their own devices.
13 If only they’d listen! If Israel would just follow my ways,
14I’d quickly subdue their enemies;
I’d turn my hand against their foes,
15I’d doom forever those who hate me while pretending to obey me.
16 I want to feed you with the finest wheat
and satisfy you with wild honey from the rocky cliffs.” Ps 81:11-16

Psalms Chapter 82 A Psalm of Asaph
1 God presides over the divine council
and judges you judges.
2So how long will youpl judge unjustly
by showingpl partiality to lawbreakers? 3 Renderpl justice to the weak and fatherless;
standpl up for the oppressed and destitute.
4 Rescuepl the weak and needy;
deliverpl them from bad people.
Ps 82:1-4
5 You don’t know or understand;
You’re walking around in the dark;
the very foundations of your world are unstable.
6 I say, “You’re gods [Jn 10:34],
children of the Most High,
7but you’ll die like other mortals
and fall like anyone else.”
8 You judge the world, God!
You’re the One that owns the nations. Ps 82:5-8

content:
Psalms Chapter 83 A Song. A Psalm of Asaph
1 God, don’t keep quiet; don’t be silent.
2 Your enemies are making an uproar;
those who hate you are exalting themselves.
3 They’re plotting against your people,
conspiring against them 4 and saying, “Let’s wipe out their nation
so no one will remember them anymore.”
5 Together they’re signing a treaty against you:
6 Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites;
7Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek;
Philistia and the people in Tyre;
8Assyria has joined them too;
they’re allied with Lot’s descendants. Ps 83:1-8 9 Deal with them like you dealt with Midian,
with Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon River,
10that you destroyed at En-dor,
that became like manure on the ground.
11 Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb and their officials like Zebah and Zalmunna,
12who said, “Let’s take over God’s pastures.” Ps 83:9-12
13 Make them like whirling dust, like chaff in the wind.
14 Like a wildfire that burns a whole forest,
like a flame that sets mountains on fire;
15chase them with your storm;
terrify them with your tempest.
16 Write shame all over their faces
till they submit to you, LORD.
17 Frighten them forever;
let them die in disgrace
18so they’ll know that you
are supreme over the whole world.
Ps 83:13-18

Psalms Chapter 84 For the Choir Director. A Psalm of the Sons of Korah
Set to The Gittith
1 Your Temple is so beautiful, LORD of Hosts!
2I long, yes, even faint with longing for your courts;
my body and soul sing for joy to the living God.
3 Even a sparrow finds a home for herself, a swallow builds a nest to raise her young
near your altars, LORD of Hosts, my God and King.
4 How blessed they are who live in your Temple
and continually sing your praises. 5 How blessed people are whose strength comes from you,
who’ve resolved to make pilgrimages to Zion!
6 As they pass through the Valley of Weeping, they turn it into a spring;
autumn rains cover it with blessings.
7 They grow from strength to more strength
till each one appears before God in Zion.
Ps 84:1-7
8 LORD God of Hosts, listen to my prayer;
listen to me, God of Jacob! 9 Extend your favor to the shield you anointed over us, 10because one day in your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere.
I’d rather stand at the threshold of your Temple
than live at ease in the tents of sinners,
11because the LORD is sun and shield,
who gives grace and honor
and doesn’t withhold anything good from those who do what’s right. 12 LORD of Hosts, how blessed they are who trust in you! Ps 84:8-12

content:
Psalms Chapter 85 For the Choir Director. A Psalm of the Sons of Korah
1 LORD, you blessed your land;
you restored the fortunes of Jacob;
2you forgave your people’s iniquity
and pardoned their sins;
3you withdrew your fury
and turned away from your hot anger.
4 Restore us, our Deliverer;
end your displeasure with us.
5 Will you be angry with us forever?
Will you extend your wrath to every generation?
6 Won’t you revive us
so we can celebrate over you?
7 Show us your enduring love, LORD;
grant us your salvation. Ps 85:1-7
8 I’ll listen to what our God the LORD says,
because he offers peace to his holy people, those who avoid foolish behavior.
9 His salvation is nearby for those who respect him,
so there can be honor in our land.
10 Truth and enduring love combine;
goodness and peace kiss each other.
11 Faithfulness grows up from the ground,
and goodness looks down from the sky.
12 The LORD gives what’s good
so our land can yield its produce.
13 Goodness goes ahead of him
and makes his footprints into a path.
Ps 85:8-13

content:
Psalms Chapter 86 A Prayer of David
1 Listen, LORD, and answer me
because I’m troubled and in need.
2 Preserve my life because I’m a godly man;
save me because I trust in you.
3 Be gracious to me because I call out to you all the time.
4 Make me happy
because I hold up my life to you.
5 You’re good, ready to forgive,
and abundant in enduring love to everyone that calls on you.
6 Hear my prayer, LORD; listen to my petition.
7 When I’m in trouble, I call on you
because you answer me.
8 There’s no one like you among the gods,
no other deeds like yours.
9 All the nations you’ve made will come to worship you and honor you,
10because you’re great and do great things;
only you are God. Ps 86:1-10
11 Teach me your way;
I’ll follow your truth;
make me consistently respect you.
12 I’ll thank you, LORD my God, with all my heart
and honor you forever
13 because you show me such enduring love;
you’ve rescued me from the depths of Sheol.
Ps 86:11-13
14 Arrogant people are attacking me, God;
a gang of violent men wants to kill me;
they don’t care about you.
15 But you’re a merciful, gracious God,
slow to get angry and abundant in enduring love and faithfulness.
16 Turn to me and be gracious;
give me your strength;
save your servant’s son.
17 Show me a sign of your favor
so the ones that hate me can see it and be put to shame,
because you’ve helped me and reassured me. Ps 86:14-17
title: Psalms 86

Philistia, Tyre, and Nubia too:

content:
Psalms Chapter 88 For the Choir Director. A Psalm of the Sons of Korah.
A Song. Set to Mahalath Leannoth
A Maskil of Herman the Ezrahite
1 LORD God who keeps me safe,
I call out to you day and night.
2 Let my prayer come to you;
listen to my call!
3 I’ve had so much trouble;
I’m close to Sheol.
4 I’m as good as dead,
like someone with no strength left.
5 Abandoned among the dead
like someone slain in the grave, I’m forgotten and cut off from you.
6 You’ve put me in the Pit, in regions dark and deep.
7 Your anger overwhelms me;
wave after wave weighs heavily on me. 8 You’ve made my friends avoid me
by making me someone they detest;
I’m trapped and can’t escape.
9 My sight is blurry from tears;
I call on you every day, LORD,
and reach out to you for help. Ps 88:1-9
10 Do you perform wonders for the dead?
Do departed spirits rise and praise you? 11 Do they declare your enduring love in the grave
or your faithfulness in the place of destruction?
12 Are your wonders known in the dark
or your goodness in the land of forgetfulness?
Ps 88:10-12
13 LORD, I call out to you for help; in the mornings my prayers go up to you.
14 Why are you rejecting me?
Why are you hiding from me?
15 I’ve been attacked and close to death from my youth up;
I suffer from the terrors you bring; I’m overwhelmed.
16 Your furious anger has swept over me;
your dreaded assaults have destroyed me.
17 They surround me like water all the time
and engulf me completely.
18 You’ve removed lover and friend far from me;
my companions lie in darkness. Ps 88:13-18
title: Psalms 88

content:
Psalms Chapter 90 BOOK 4 A Prayer of Moses, the Man of God
1 LORD, through all generations
you’ve been our dwelling place.
2 Before the mountains were born
or you gave birth to the world,
from one end of time to the other, you’ve been God. Ps 90:1-2
3 You turn people back to dust and say, “Return to dust, mortals.”
4 A thousand years to you
are like yesterday,
like a watch in the night.
5 You sweep us away like the dreams in our sleep.
In the morning we sprout like grass 6 and flourish;
then toward evening we fade like blossoms
and wither away.
7 Your anger consumes us;
your wrath scares us.
8 You place our iniquities in front of you; our secret sins are open to you.
9 All our days pass away in your fury;
we finish our years with a sigh.
10 We live for 70 years or by good health for 80 years;
yet whatever their length, they’re full of labor and pain
because they’re gone so soon, and we fly away.
11 Who understands the power of your anger and fury
in comparison to the respect you deserve?
12 So teach us to count our days
so we can grow in wisdom toward you. Ps 90:3-12
13 Come back to us, LORD; how long will it be?
Have pity on your servants.
14 Satisfy us in the morning with your enduring love
so we can sing and be happy our whole life.
15 Make us happy for as long as you’ve punished us,
for the years we’ve had misfortune.
16 Let us see your work
and our children witness your majesty.
17 Bless us, LORD our God;
make our efforts successful;
yes, make them succeed! Ps 90:13-17

Psalms Chapter 91 1 Those who live in the shelter of the Most High
will find rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
2 They’ll say about the LORD, “Our refuge and fortress, the God we trust!” Ps 91:1-2
3 He delivers you from the trapper’s snare
and deadly pestilence.
4He covers you with his pinions;
you can find refuge under his wings;
his faithfulness shields and protects you.
5 You won’t be afraid of terrors at night,
of arrows that fly by day,
6 of pestilence that lurks in the dark,
or destruction that lays waste at noon.
7 A thousand may fall at your side, ten thousand by your right hand;
but disaster won’t touch you.
8 You’ll stand by and watch his recompense to the wicked,
9because you’ve made the LORD your refuge,
the Most High your hiding place.
10 Misfortune won’t fall on you;
no plague will get near you. Ps 91:3-10
11 He’ll make his angels responsible for guarding you whatever you do.
12 They’ll carry you so you won’t trip over a rock [Mt 4:6; Lk 4:10-11].
13 You’ll step on lions and cobras
and crush them.
14 “I’ll rescue them that love me
and set up high those who know me.
15 They’ll call on me, and I’ll answer them;
I’ll be with them in trouble,
rescue and honor them.
16 I’ll satisfy them with long life
and give them salvation.” Ps 91:11-16

Psalms Chapter 92 A Psalm
A Song for the Sabbath
1 It’s good to thank you, LORD,
to sing praises to you, Most High;
2 to declare your enduring love in the morning
and your faithfulness at night
3 with a lute and a ten-stringed harp,
with melody on a lyre.
4Because you’ve made me happy by what you’ve done,
I’ll sing for joy over what you do. Ps 92:1-4
5 Your deeds are so great, LORD,
your thoughts so deep!
6 Senseless people don’t realize,
ignorant mortals don’t understand 7 that when sinners sprout up like grass
and the wicked flourish,
it’s only that they’ll be destroyed forever.
8 But you’re on high forever.
9 Your enemies will perish;
everybody that sins will scatter. Ps 92:5-9
10 You’ve made me as strong as a wild ox
and anointed me with fresh oil.
11 I’ve looked in triumph at my enemies
and heard about the defeat of my attackers.
12 Good people flourish like palm trees;
they grow like cedars in Lebanon.
13 Planted in the LORD’s Temple,
they flourish in the courts of our God.
14 They bear fruit even when they’re old;
they’re still green and full of energy.
15They declare that the LORD is good,
that he’s our rock; there’s nothing bad about him. Ps 92:10-15

Psalms Chapter 94 1 LORD God of vengeance, shine!
2 Rise up, Judge of the whole world;
repay the proud.
3 How long will you let sinners celebrate?
4 How long will they pour out their arrogant words,
vaunt themselves up
5crush your people, attack your heritage
6murder widows and foreigners and orphans,
7and say, “The LORD’s not watching;
Jacob’s God is not paying attention.” Ps 94:1-7
8 You silly people, you pay attention;
when will you ever understand?
9 Can’t he hear, who created the ear?
Can’t he see, who formed the eye?
10 Won’t he that rebukes nations, discipline you;
doesn’t the Source of knowledge know what you’re doing?
11 The LORD knows that your thoughts are nothing but hot air [1 Cor 3:20].
12 The ones you discipline are blessed, LORD,
the ones you teach out of the Law; 13 so you can grant them relief in adversity,
till you dig a pit for the wicked. 14 The LORD won’t abandon his people
or forsake his inheritance.
15 The administration of justice will be good again,
and the godly will follow it.
16 Who else will stand up for me against evil people?
Who else will take a stand for me against sinners?
Ps 94:8-16
17 If the LORD hadn’t helped me,
I would soon have occupied the silent place.
18When I cried out, “I’m slipping,”
his enduring love kept me from falling.
19When my anxious thoughts multiplied,
he cheered me up.
20 Can corrupt rulers be his allies
and plot schemes with their wicked laws?
21 Can they gang up on good people
and condemn the innocent to death?
22 No, because the LORD is my fortress;
my God the Rock is my refuge.
23 He’ll bring their sinfulness back on them
and destroy them with their own evil;
the LORD our God will wipe them out. Ps 94:17-23

Psalms Chapter 95 1 Come, let’s sing to the LORD;
let’s make a joyful sound to the Rock that saves us.
2 Let’s go to him with thanksgiving
and sing to him with psalms.
3 The LORD is a great God,
a great King above all gods.
4 He controls the deep sea;
he owns the mountain peaks 5and the ocean because he created them;
he made the dry land. Ps 95:1-5
6 Come, let’s bow in worship;
let’s kneel to the LORD our Maker.

Psalms Chapter 101 A Psalm of David
1 I’ll sing about your enduring love and justice,
and sing praises to you, LORD.
2 I’ll pay attention to the way that’s blameless;
when will you come to help me?
In my home I’ll walk in integrity.
3 I won’t set anything base beside me;
I’ll hate what they do who fall away;
I’ll stay away from them.
4 I’ll cast perverse things out of my heart
and have nothing to do with evil.
5 I’ll withdraw from anyone that slanders another;
I won’t put up with people that have haughty looks or arrogant hearts.
Ps 101:1-5
6 I’ll focus my attention on the faithful to be my friends.
Those who follow the blameless way are the ones that will be my servants.
7 I won’t let deceivers serve in my Temple;
liars won’t maintain their relationship with me.
8 Each morning I’ll destroy the wicked in the land
and rid the city of the LORD of everyone that sins.
Ps 101:6-8
title: Psalms 101

Psalms Chapter 102 A Prayer by the Oppressed When They’re Faint and Pour Out Their Complaint to the LORD
1 Listen to my prayer, LORD!
Let my cry come to you.
2 Don’t turn away from me in my distress;
when I call, answer quickly.
3 My days dissipate like smoke;
my bones lie scorched on a hearth.
4 My heart is weak and withers away like grass;
I have no appetite 5 in my loud groaning;
I’m skin and bones.
6 I’m like a pelican in the desert,
like an owl in desolate places; 7 I lie awake
like a lonely bird on a housetop. Ps 102:1-7
8 My enemies taunt me all day; they ridicule me and use my name as a curse.
9 I eat ashes for food
and mix my drink with tears
10because of your indignation,
because you’ve thrown me away.
11 My days are like a shadow;
I wither like the grass.
12 But you live forever, LORD;
you endure for all generations.
13 Have mercy on Zion;
it’s time to be gracious to it;
the appointed time has come.
14 Your servants delight in its very rocks
and have regard even for its dust.
15 So the nations will respect the LORD;
kings will respect your honor.
16 The LORD will build up Zion;
he’ll appear in his glory.
17 He’ll have regard for the destitute;
he won’t disregard their prayer.
Ps 102:8-17
18 Write this for the next generation,
so people not yet born will praise the LORD:
19 He looked down from his holy height;
from heaven he gazed at earth
20to hear the groaning prisoners,
to free those doomed to die;
21so people will celebrate the LORD in Zion
and praise him in Jerusalem
22when the nations gather
and the kingdoms assemble to serve him. Ps 102:18-22
23 He weakened my strength in the course of my life and shortened it.
24 I say to him,
My God, don’t take me away in the middle of life;
you live throughout all generations.
25You founded the earth long ago;
the sky is your handiwork.
26Even they will perish, but you’ll remain;
they’ll wear out like a robe,

Psalms Chapter 103 A Psalm of David
1 Bless the LORD, all that I am!
Everything that’s in me, bless him.
2 Bless the LORD, all that I am;
May I never forget how he helps me: 3he pardons my sins
and heals my diseases;
4he rescues me from the Pit
and crowns me with enduring love and mercy;
5he satisfies my years with good things,
and renews my youth like an eagle’s.
Ps 103:1-5
6 The LORD performs good deeds
and renders justice for people mistreated.
7 He made his ways known to Moses
and demonstrated his acts to Israel.
8 The LORD is merciful and gracious,
slow to anger and abounding in enduring love.
9 He won’t constantly confront us
or always be angry with us.
10 He hasn’t dealt with us according to our sins
or rewarded us in proportion to our iniquities.
11 As high as the sky is above the earth,
so great is his enduring love toward those who respect him.
12 As far as the east is from the west,
that’s how far he’s removed our sins from us.
13 Like a father that has mercy on his children,
the LORD has mercy on those who respect him.
14 He knows how we’re made;
he’s aware that we’re only dust. Ps 103:6-14
15 People are like grass,
they flourish like flowers in a field.
16 When the wind blows on them, they’re gone
like they’d never been there.
17 The LORD’s enduring love is from eternity past to future for them who respect him; his goodness is to children’s children
18to those who keep his covenant,
that obey his commandments. Ps 103:15-18
19 The LORD has secured his throne in the sky;
he’s sovereign everywhere.
20 Bless the LORD, angels, great in power, who do what he says and obey him.
21 Bless the LORD, all his hosts
who serve him and do his will.
22 Bless the LORD, everything he’s created
everywhere he reigns.
Bless the LORD, everything that I am! Ps 103:19-22
title: Psalms 103

Psalms Chapter 104 1 Bless the LORD, everything that I am!
LORD my God, you’re so great;
you’re dressed in splendor and majesty.
2 You cover yourself with light as with a robe;
you’ve stretched out the sky like a tent.
3 You laid the beams for your rooms on the water;
you make the clouds your chariot
and walk on the wind.
4 You make your messengers winds
and your ministers a blazing fire [Heb 1:7]. Ps 104:1-4
5 You built the earth on foundations
so it would never shift. 6 You covered it with the ocean like a robe
deeper than the mountains.
7 At your rebuke it receded;
at the sound of your thunder, it withdrew.
8 The mountains rose up; the valleys sank down to the level you determined for them to have.
9 You set a boundary the water couldn’t cross
so it wouldn’t flow back over the earth again. Ps 104:5-9
10 You make springs in the valleys
so creeks flow between the mountains.
11 They water the animals in the countryside
and quench the thirst of wild donkeys.
12 Birds live beside them
and chirp in the trees.
13 You water the mountains from your home above;
your work provides for the earth. Ps 104:10-13
14 You make grass grow for the livestock
and crops from people’s labor
so they could produce food from the ground
15 and wine to cheer them up,
so they could make their faces shine with oil
and grow food to sustain them.
16 The LORD’s trees drink their fill,
Lebanon’s cedars that he planted,
17 where birds build their nests
and storks make roosts in fir trees. Ps 104:14-17
18 High mountains are for wild goats, and rocks provide cover for badgers.
19 You made the moon to mark the seasons;
the sun knows where to set.
20 You send darkness, and it becomes night;
wild animals prowl around in it.
21 Young lions roar after their prey
and seek their food from God.
22 When the sun comes up, they go back and lie down in their dens,
23and people go out to work till evening. Ps 104:18-23
24 LORD, how many things you’ve done!
you’ve done them all with wisdom
and filled the earth …

Psalms Chapter 105 1 Be grateful to the LORD; call on him;
tell the nations what all he’s done.
2 Sing praises to him;
talk about the amazing acts.
3 Take pride in his holy name;
let the people be happy that rely on him.
4 Rely on the LORD and his strength;
depend on him always.
5 Remember his amazing miracles,
the judgments he’s rendered,
6 descendants of Abraham his servant,
children of Jacob, his chosen ones!
7 He’s the LORD our God,
who renders judgment all over the world. Ps 105:1-7
8 He remembers his eternal covenant,
the message he commanded to a thousand generations,
9 his covenant with Abraham, his oath to Isaac.
10his statute confirmed to Jacob
as an ongoing covenant.
11 He swore, “I’ll give you Canaan to inherit.”
12 When they were just a few,
temporary residents,
13they wandered from nation to nation,
from kingdom to kingdom.
14 He didn’t let anybody oppress them;
he reprimanded kings on their behalf:
15“Don’t touch my anointed ones;
don’t harm my prophets.” Ps 105:8-15
16 He called for a famine in the land
and cut off their food supply.
17 He sent a man ahead of them,
Joseph, sold as a slave.
18 They hurt his feet with restraints
and put an iron collar around his neck
19 till God’s message came to him
and revealed what kind of man he was.
20 The king released him;
the people’s ruler let him go.
21 He made him master of his household,
steward over everything he owned,
22 even to imprison his officials if he saw fit
so he could teach his elders wisdom. Ps 105:16-22
23 Then Israel/Jacob went down to Egypt
and lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.
24 God multiplied his people and made them stronger than their enemies,
25whose hearts he turned against his people to mistreat them. 26 Then he sent Moses his servant
and Aaron his chosen one
27to perform his amazing acts among them,
miracles in the land of Ham:
28he engulfed their land in darkness
when they defied him and his message;
29he turned their water to blood
and killed their fish; Ps 105:23-29 …

Be grateful to the LORD because he’s good; his enduring love lasts forever.
2 Who can recount all his mighty deeds?
Who can ever praise him enough?
3 How blessed they are who maintain justice,
who practice goodness all the time!
4 Remember me, LORD, when you’re gracious to your people; come and rescue me
5so I can share in your holy people’s prosperity,
celebrate in your nation’s happiness,
and glory in your heritage. Ps 106:1-5
6 We and our ancestors have sinned, committed iniquity, and behaved badly. 7 Our ancestors in Egypt didn’t get the point of the LORD’s amazing acts
or remember his abundant kindness;
instead, they rebelled against him at the Red Sea.
8 Nevertheless, he saved them to defend his honor
and demonstrate his power.
9 He commanded the Red Sea to dry up,
and led them through its depths as through a desert.
10 He saved them from those who hated them;
he rescued them from their enemy.
11 The water drowned their adversaries;
not a one survived.
12 Then they believed in him and praised him in song. Ps 106:6-12

and didn’t wait for his direction,

but sent a wasting disease among them. Ps 106:13-15

and of Aaron, the LORD’s holy priest,

content:
Psalms Chapter 107 BOOK 5 1 Be grateful to the LORD because he’s good;
his love endures forever.
2 Let his redeemed say it, the ones he rescued from their adversaries 3 and gathered from other countries
east and west, north and south. Ps 107:1-3
4 Some wandered in trackless desert
and couldn’t find their way to any inhabited city.
5 Hungry and thirsty,
their souls fainted inside them.
6 Then they appealed to the LORD in their trouble,
and he delivered them from it;
7 he led them straight to a city they could live in.
8They need to thank him for his enduring love
and his awesome acts for his people!
9 He satisfies the thirsty and fills the hungry with good things. Ps 107:4-9
10 Some sat in darkness and death’s shadow,
prisoners suffering in iron shackles,
11 because they’d rebelled against what God said
and spurned the advice of the Most High.
12 So he humbled them with labor;
they stumbled and nobody was there to help.
13 Then they appealed to the LORD in their trouble,
and he delivered them from it.
14 He brought them out of darkness and death’s shadow
and broke their chains.
15They need to thank him for his enduring love
and his awesome acts for his people!
16 because he shattered bronze gates
and cut iron bars in two. Ps 107:10-16
17 Some were fools and suffered because they rebelled and sinned.
18 The very sight of food was repulsive to them;
they came close to dying.

content:
Psalms Chapter 110 A Psalm of David
1 The LORD said to my Lord,
“Sit at my right hand
till I make your enemies your footstool” [Mt 22:44; Mk 12:36; 14:62; Lk 20:42; 22:69; Acts 2:34; Heb 1:13].
2 The LORD will extend your mighty scepter from on Zion, and say, “Rule your enemies.”
3 Your soldiers will volunteer readily
when you muster your army in holy array;
your strength will be renewed
every morning like the dew.
4 The LORD has sworn and won’t change his mind,
“You’re a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek” [Heb 5:6, 17, 21].
5 The LORD is at your right hand
to shatter kings when it’s time to display his anger.
6 He’ll render judgment against the nations by filling them with corpses;
he’ll shatter leaders worldwide.
7 He’ll refresh himself from streams along the way
and raise up his head in triumph. Ps 110-:1-7

content:
Psalms Chapter 111 1Hallelujah!
I thank the LORD with all my heart
in the presence of his godly people.
2 His works are so outstanding
no one that delights in them can quit thinking about them;
3their splendor and majesty
reflect his eternal goodness;
4he makes his amazing acts memorable
because they show his grace and mercy.
5 He feeds those who respect him
and remembers his covenant with them;
6he demonstrated his power to his people
by giving them other nations’ land. Ps 111:1-6
7 His works are just and true;
so his people can trust his commandments
8to bring eternal security
when they practice them sincerely.
9 He has provided redemption for his people
and ordained his covenant with them forever;
he’s holy and awesome.
10 Respecting the LORD is the most important thing about being wise;
doing what he commands brings understanding.
Praise him forever. Ps 111:7-10
